ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The attached diagram shows a figure made from outlined squares. On the left bottom is a square whose bottom side is labeled 40. Directly above this 40-square are two smaller squares side by side; the left small square has a vertical side labeled 16. A much larger square is attached on the right, with its bottom aligned with the bottom of the 40-square and its top aligned with the top of the right small square above the 40-square. Reasoning: Since the lower-left square has side 40, the total width across the two top squares above it is also 40. The left top square has side 16, so the right top square has side 40 - 16 = 24. The biggest square on the right extends vertically from the bottom of the 40-square to the top of that 24-square, so its side length is 40 + 24 = 64.

method.method_draft: Set variables from the square layout. Let the side of the largest square be L and the side of the upper middle square be x. The lower-left square has side 40 because the bottom label spans its width. The upper-left square has side 16. Since the upper-left and upper-middle squares together exactly span the 40-wide lower-left square, 16 + x = 40, so x = 24. Vertically, the largest square spans the height of the 40-square plus the height x of the upper-middle square, giving L = 40 + 24 = 64.
